sessions.title: Tales of the Fisherman's Wife
sessions.desc: During the Edo period in Japan (1600-1868), kaidan stories arose from a popular parlor game called Hyakumonogatari Kaidankai, or “A Gathering of One Hundred Weird Tales.” Played in the summertime, when the sky stays lit well into the night and the air is stiflingly humid, Hyakumonogatari Kaidankai is a simple storytelling parlor game with an evocation ritual reminiscent of “Bloody Mary.” The host lights a hundred candles, and players take turns telling strange and grotesque stories, folktales, and ghost stories.Players will play a character from a small fishing village participating in this tradition. They are given a traditional folktale to read and tell the others.At the end of each story, the teller of the tale extinguishes a candle. The room darkens at the conclusion of each story, the fading light calls upon the spirits and creatures of the stories. When the final candle goes out, something monstrous may fill the darkness.

sessions.title: A Verry Merry Board Meeting
sessions.desc: You are Santa’s Elves! Each player will be taking on the character of a North Pole elf, working in one of the departments essential to making The Big Day function on behalf of The Big Guy (Good old Saint Nick, Krisingle, Santa Claus himself). The game is meant to engage solely with the secular side of the Christmas holiday, and the elves themselves do not observe Christmas.The North Pole is about to enter the busiest time of the year- it is the day after Thanksgiving, and the day of the annual Board Meeting, where all of the departments meet to go over final plans and resource allotment before the last big push. Before this meeting, the departmental work has been guided by the Heads of each department, hoping to make their goals and show their progress at the big meeting. The Heads, any Assistants, and Interns (it’s a good learning opportunity!) are the only elves who attend and will later direct the other elves in what needs to be done. The big decision to be made is who is going to handle Wrapping, as there is no department who has direct oversight of the increasingly difficult job. Everything must be decided by the time the Big Guy visits the meeting.Elves are never negative about anything. Everything is the best idea ever. No one has ever done anything wrong. Everyone is just the bestest of friends. All problems can be fixed, and no one should ever be without a smile. Some elves have managed to turn this positivity into a shield or a weapon, while others long to break free of its grasp- but doing so would undoubtedly have terrible social and career consequences. Not all elves like each other, and there are tensions between many of the departments and sometimes even within the department. Some elves are stuck doing jobs they have come to despise, and others are just sick of keeping up appearances.So have the very merriest of board meetings, my elfin friends! I’m sure it’s all going to go just wonderfully!
